The PV075 is a SuperVent air eliminator from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 3/4 in female NPT connection, 13 Cv.

Why air has to come out of a hydronic loop. Fresh fill water carries dissolved air, and heating it drives that air out of solution. What it does next is all bad: it collects at high points and blocks flow, it gasses through the circulator as noise, it puts oxygen against steel where there was none, and it turns a radiator into a cold half-radiator. A system that has to be bled every autumn is a system that is still taking air in somewhere.

An air eliminator works by slowing the water down. Inside the body the flow spreads out and loses velocity, the bubbles stop being carried along, they rise into the vent chamber, and a float valve lets them out. It runs continuously, with nothing to set and nothing to press.

Flow capacity is 13 Cv. Size the separator to the pipe it sits in, not to the boiler — an undersized body throttles the loop, and an oversized one is money spent on brass.

Threaded NPT connects to anything and comes apart again, which matters on a component that may be serviced.

Put it where the water is hottest and the pressure lowest — on the supply, close to the boiler outlet. That is where air comes out of solution most readily, and catching it there keeps it from reaching the rest of the system at all.

Body is bronze, rated to 240 F maximum and 125 psi.

The VCZAL1100 is a VC series two-way valve assembly from Resideo, the brand that carries the Honeywell Home line of residential heating controls, built for hydronic zoning and fan coil control. It is a 3/4-inch female NPT body with a 4.7 Cv rating and a linear flow characteristic.

A linear characteristic means flow tracks stem position in a straight line, which keeps a modulating loop stable instead of dumping most of its capacity in the first part of the stroke.

What a complete VC zone valve takes: a valve body, a cartridge, and an actuator, ordered separately. This listing is the valve assembly — pick the actuator that matches your control signal, whether that is two-position, floating, or modulating.

Building the valve from separate parts is what makes the VC platform worth specifying: the same body stays in the pipe while the actuator is matched to the control system, and a worn seat is handled by pulling the cartridge rather than cutting the body out.

The CPRD10 is a constant-pressure bypass damper from Resideo (Honeywell Home), 10 in round.

A bypass damper is what keeps a zoned system from destroying itself. When only one small zone calls, the blower is still moving the air it was sized for and it has nowhere to put it: static pressure climbs, ducts boom, the coil freezes on cooling and the heat exchanger cooks on heating. The bypass opens against that pressure and returns the surplus.

This one is not motorized and has no wiring. A calibrated spring holds it shut and duct pressure opens it, so it reacts to the actual pressure in the duct rather than to a signal from the panel. Set the spring tension once at commissioning and it needs nothing after that.

Size the bypass to the smallest zone, not to the trunk — the case it has to handle is one small zone calling alone.
